notes:
Futa Toro (Denianke kingdom 1513-1776, Imamate 1776-1859), additions batch af-03-x; no Cliopatria row. One state, one dossier: the 1776 change is a rename event.

Date conflicts: start 1513 (Jolof page) versus 1512 (Denianke page dynasty list); end 1859 (Imamate infobox and "annexed by France in 1859") versus 1891 (the text's end of resistance); Abdul Kader's reign 1776-1804 (infobox) versus death in 1806 (text); Samba Lamu's apex (page text versus ruler list 1565-67). The Denianke page ranks Futa Djallon and Bambouk as falling under Denianke control by the late 16th century; this contradicts the Futa Jallon and Bambuk histories and is not drawn. The Takrur dossier (af-03-a) ends in 1285; the land was Mali's, then Jolof's.

No area on any page; the north-bank extent (Chemama) is the Gorgol valley by reading. No rulers strip: the Denianke list on the page is partial (gaps 1565-1603, 1640-1669, 1702-1724 ...). Tributary list is dated only "by the end of the 16th century" and "early 17th century" (Cayor); the end of the tribute is a bridge (1776, confidence 1).

Counterparts needing dossiers: jolof-kingdom, cayor, waalo, saloum, gajaaga (the Soninke kingdom on the upper Senegal), the Trarza and Brakna emirates, Bundu. Gazetteer names needed: Orefonde, Tumbere-Jiinde, Chemama (region), Gajaaga.

Revised 2026-10-19 after the review (verdict fail): (a) The shape is the middle valley strip, not the gazetteer region 'Futa Toro' plus Matam and Gorgol (76,000 km2): {intersect: [Senegal river 40 km, box 15.5-12.5 W x 15.5-16.8 N]} minus the Saint-Louis admin1 (waalo's stand-in), about 15,000 km2, drawn from the Futa Toro page's 'about 400 km long, fertile land up to 20 km each side of the river'. Cut named: Podor and Toro lie in Saint-Louis and are left to waalo's proxy; a gazetteer fix of 'Futa Toro' (its box starts at the Atlantic) is requested. (b) The Denianke tribute is split into one vassal_start per tributary (jolof-kingdom, waalo, saloum, gajaaga, diarra at 1599, c2; cayor at 1610, c1) with the vassal_end of 1776 (c1); Fatick is out. Diakhaba, Goundiourou, Namandirou and the Lamtuna are on the page's list but have no dossier in this batch; Khasso, listed only as possible, has one (khasso) and no event is recorded for it. (c) End of the tribute: the Abdul Kader Kane page, re-read, does not discuss tribute, so 1776 stays a bridge. (d) The infobox 'Incorporated into Senegal Colony: 1877' is noted on the 1859 events; the 1859 annexation remains the end.
